client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: Immediately after using a contaminated needle, what should the nurse do?

options.A: Recap it with two hands before disposal
options.B: Place it immediately or as soon as feasible in an appropriate sharps container without recapping
options.C: Leave it on the tray until the end of the medication pass
options.D: Discard it into regular trash if the needle appears intact

rationale: OSHA requires contaminated sharps to be discarded immediately or as soon as feasible in closable, puncture-resistant, leakproof, labeled or color-coded sharps containers. Contaminated needles generally must not be recapped.
educational_objective: Dispose of a used contaminated needle promptly in a compliant sharps container without routine recapping.
source_claim_supported: Contaminated needles generally must not be recapped and contaminated sharps must be discarded immediately/as soon as feasible into compliant sharps containers.

correction_summary: Replaced generic source metadata with the exact OSHA regulatory subsections and kept the regulatory exception out of the stem because no special procedure requiring recapping is present.
audit_findings: B is the required routine action. A conflicts with the no-recap rule; C delays disposal; D uses a noncompliant receptacle. No second answer remains.
